subtitle: Understand how to build compelling solos using motivic development, tension, and resolution.

introduction.title: Architecture of a Great Solo
introduction.text: Like a great speech or story, a memorable solo has clear structure: introduction, development, climax, and resolution. Every solo should take the listener on an emotional journey from start to finish, with peaks and valleys of intensity.

columns.title: Structure Creates Impact
columns.text: Formula: Simple theme -> Development -> Climax -> Resolution

columns.title: Emotional Journey
columns.text: Elements: Dynamics, register, rhythmic activity, harmonic complexity

cards.title: ABA Form
cards.description: Statement - Development - Restatement

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Present a theme, develop/vary it, return to original theme

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Many jazz standards, "Stairway to Heaven" solo

cards.title: Linear Build
cards.description: Gradual increase in intensity and complexity

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Start simple and sparse, build to climactic peak

fields.label: Example
fields.value: "Comfortably Numb", "November Rain"

cards.title: Call & Response
cards.description: Musical conversation between phrases

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Phrase poses question, next phrase answers

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Blues solos, "While My Guitar Gently Weeps"

cards.title: Theme & Variations
cards.description: Present theme, then create variations

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Take simple motif, vary rhythm, harmony, register

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Classical influenced rock, progressive rock

cards.title: Sequence
cards.description: Repeat motif at different pitch levels

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Play same phrase pattern starting on different scale degrees

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Creates unity while providing forward motion

cards.title: Inversion
cards.description: Flip the motif upside down

fields.label: Example
fields.value: If original goes up 3rd, down 2nd, inversion goes down 3rd, up 2nd

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Provides variation while maintaining recognizable relationship

cards.title: Rhythmic Displacement
cards.description: Change when the motif starts in the measure

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Move motif from beat 1 to beat 2, or start on upbeat

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Creates syncopation and rhythmic interest

cards.title: Augmentation/Diminution
cards.description: Change the note durations of the motif

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Play same notes twice as fast or twice as slow

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Maintains melodic content while changing energy level

cards.title: Modal Transformation
cards.description: Change the mode/scale context of the motif

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Play major motif in minor, or add chromatic alterations

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Maintains structure while changing emotional color

cards.title: Harmonic Tension
cards.description: Tension and resolution is what makes music emotionally compelling. Without tension, music sounds boring. Without resolution, it sounds chaotic.

fields.label: Non-chord tones
fields.value: Use notes outside current chord -> Resolve to chord tones

fields.label: Chromatic approach
fields.value: Approach chord tones from half-step away -> Land on chord tone

fields.label: Suspended notes
fields.value: Use 4ths and 2nds instead of 3rds -> Resolve suspension to 3rd

cards.title: Rhythmic Tension
cards.description: Creating rhythmic contrast and surprise through timing manipulation.

fields.label: Syncopation
fields.value: Accent off-beats or weak beats -> Return to strong beat emphasis

fields.label: Cross-rhythms
fields.value: Play in different time feel than backing -> Realign with main rhythm

fields.label: Metric modulation
fields.value: Temporarily suggest different tempo -> Return to original tempo feel

cards.title: Register Tension
cards.description: Using pitch range to create and resolve musical tension.

fields.label: High register
fields.value: Move to highest frets for intensity -> Return to middle register

fields.label: Wide leaps
fields.value: Large interval jumps create surprise -> Stepwise motion provides rest

fields.label: Range extremes
fields.value: Use very high and very low notes -> Return to comfortable range

cards.title: Analyze
cards.description: Study chord progression, key, and song structure

cards.title: Create Motif
cards.description: Develop 2-4 note musical idea that fits the harmony

cards.title: Plan Structure
cards.description: Decide on overall form and emotional arc

cards.title: Develop
cards.description: Use motivic techniques to create variations

cards.title: Build Climax
cards.description: Create peak moment using tension techniques

cards.title: Resolve
cards.description: Bring tension to satisfying conclusion

practiceSection.title: Solo Construction Exercises
items: Motif Development: Create a simple 3-note motif. Spend 10 minutes developing it using sequence, inversion, and rhythmic displacement. Forces you to create variety from minimal material.
Structure Practice: Record a simple chord progression. Create 3 different solo structures over the same progression. Develops understanding of how structure affects impact.
Tension Exercise: Play a solo that builds tension for 8 bars, then resolves in 4 bars. Focus on harmonic and rhythmic tension. Teaches control of musical tension and release.
